title: 1985 AHSME Problem 28
statement: In \(\triangle ABC,\) we have \(\angle C=3\angle A,\) \(a=27\) and \(c=48.\) What is \(b?\)

solutions.text: By the sine law and the triple-angle identity, \[ \frac{48}{27} =\frac{\sin3A}{\sin A} =3-4\sin^2A. \] Hence \(\sin^2A=\frac{11}{36}.\) Since \(A\lt60^\circ,\) \(\cos A=\frac{5}{6},\) and therefore \(\cos2A=\frac{7}{18}.\) Also \(B=180^\circ-4A,\) so another application of the sine law gives \[ \begin{aligned} b &=27\frac{\sin B}{\sin A}\\ &=27\frac{\sin4A}{\sin A}\\ &=27\cdot4\cos A\cos2A\\ &=35. \end{aligned} \] Thus the correct answer is B.
hints: Use the sine law to write \(\frac{48}{27}=\frac{\sin3A}{\sin A}\)
After finding \(\cos A,\) use \(B=180^\circ-4A\) and \(\sin4A=4\sin A\cos A\cos2A\)
